deities: Sree Valayanad Bhagavathy (Chandika; from Kashmir, known as Mahartham and Kalasarppini)
Sapthamathrukkal (seven mother goddesses, carved in wood on the sanctum's southern wall)
festivals: Annual festival in Makaram (January-February), starting on Karthika star, for seven days; includes Pallivetta and Arat at Trissaala kulam, Mankavu
Kalamezhuthupattu (from 1st Vrichikam for 41 days during the Mandala season)

history.summary: Sree Valayanad Devi Temple at Valayanad, Kozhikode, is the family temple of the Zamorin Swaroopam (the Samoothiri rulers of medieval Kozhikode) and one of the rare Saktheya temples where worship follows the Rurujit practice. Legend says the Zamorin was repeatedly defeated by Valluvakonathiri of Valluvanad despite superior military strength; realizing the Devi's blessings lay with his foe, he undertook tapas at the Thirumandhamkunnu temple until Bhagavathy appeared and agreed to accompany him home, on condition he never look back. When he did, she threw her bangle, declaring her presence would rest where it fell; the bangle orbited for a week (Azhcha) before landing, giving the names Azhchavattom and Thiruvalayanad. The temple is traditionally dated to the 14th century and built by the Zamorins; it is dedicated to Bhagavathy as Chandika, a goddess from Kashmir also called Mahartham and Kalasarppini, and the Sreechakra in the sanctum is attributed to the Sivayogi Thayyavur Sivasankar. Poojas follow the rare Kularnava Tantra and are performed by Pidarar/Moosad priests, of whom five illams hold the hereditary right; the temple is noted for its wooden carvings of the Sapthamathrukkal and its copper-covered roofs in Kerala style.

name: Sree Valayanadu Devi Temple
town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is the historic spice-trade port city of the Malabar Coast in northern Kerala, once the capital of the Zamorins and dubbed the 'City of Spices' for its medieval role in Eastern spice commerce. Today it blends colonial-era landmarks and beaches such as Kappad with a thriving food culture and serves as the gateway to the temples of Malabar.

travel.airport: Calicut International Airport at Karipur (approx. 21-28 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Kozhikode Main Railway Station (approx. 3-4 km), on the Shoranur-Mangalore section; Kallayi station is about 1 km from the temple.
travel.road: On the Mankavu-Govindapuram route, Valayanad Temple Road, about 3 km southeast of Kozhikode city (Palayam junction); Valayanad bus stop is about 150 m from the temple. City buses, autos and taxis reach it easily; off the mini-bypass on NH66.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; the annual festival in Makaram (January-February) is the grandest time, with thousands of devotees. Tuesdays and Fridays are considered the most auspicious days for worship.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning from about 5:00 AM (Nirmalyam at 5:06 AM per the temple's official site) to about 12:00 noon; evening from 5:30 PM to about 8:00 PM (verify closing time - listings vary between 8:00 PM and 9:00 PM). No entry fee; observe Kerala temple dress codes (men remove shirts inside the sanctum area).
